questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality Involving an Odd Power
questions.worked_solution:
Isolating the ninth-degree term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}3(2-5x)^{9}+5 & \le 8 \\ 3(2-5x)^{9} & \le 3 \\ (2-5x)^{9} & \le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the ninth root of both sides and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[9]{(2-5x)^{9}} & \le \sqrt[9]{1} \\ 2-5x & \le 1 \\ -5x & \le -1 \\ x & \ge \frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-6)^{3}+5 & \le 0 \\ (x-6)^{3} & \le -5.\end{aligned}

Then, we take the third root of both sides and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{(x-6)^{3}} & \le \sqrt[3]{-5} \\ x-6 & \le \sqrt[3]{-5} \\ x & \le \sqrt[3]{-5}+6.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality Involving an Even Power
questions.worked_solution:
Isolating the sixth-degree term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}4(1-x)^{6}-1 & >7 \\ 4(1-x)^{6} & >8 \\ (1-x)^{6} & >2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take the sixth root of both sides and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[6]{(1-x)^{6}} & >\sqrt[6]{2} \\ |1-x| & >\sqrt[6]{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
1-x<-\sqrt[6]{2}\,\text{or}\,1-x>\sqrt[6]{2}
$$

We can solve each inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}1-x & <-\sqrt[6]{2} &  &  & 1-x & >\sqrt[6]{2} \\ -x & <-\sqrt[6]{2}-1 &  &  & -x & >\sqrt[6]{2}-1 \\ x & >1+\sqrt[6]{2} &  &  & x & <1-\sqrt[6]{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is

$$
x<1-\sqrt[6]{2}\,\text{or}\,x>1+\sqrt[6]{2}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality Involving an Even Power
questions.worked_solution:
Isolating the sixth-degree term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}-4(5-x)^{6}+147 & >-109 \\ -4(5-x)^{6} & >-256 \\ (5-x)^{6} & <64.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we had to flip the inequality when we divided both sides by $-4.$

Now, we take the sixth root of both sides and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[6]{(5-x)^{6}} & <\sqrt[6]{64} \\ |5-x| & <2.\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
-2<5-x<2
$$

Now, we can solve the compound inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}-2<5-x & <2 \\ -7<-x & <-3 \\ 7>x & >3\end{aligned}
$$

To make the final result easier to read, we will rewrite it so that the lower number is on the left:

$$
3<x<7
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality Involving an Even Power
questions.worked_solution:
Isolating the quadratic term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}(5-x)^{2}+4 & \le 6 \\ (5-x)^{2} & \le 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take the square root of both sides and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{(5-x)^{2}} & \le \sqrt{2} \\ |5-x| & \le \sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
-\sqrt{2}\le 5-x\le \sqrt{2}
$$

Now, we can solve the compound inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{2}\le 5-x & \le \sqrt{2} \\ -\sqrt{2}-5\le -x & \le \sqrt{2}-5 \\ 5+\sqrt{2}\ge x & \ge 5-\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To make the final result easier to read, we will rewrite it so that the lower number is on the left:

$$
5-\sqrt{2}\le x\le 5+\sqrt{2}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Isolating the quadratic term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}(4-x)^{2}-10 & \ge 7 \\ (4-x)^{2} & \ge 17.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take the square root of both sides and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{(4-x)^{2}} & \ge \sqrt{17} \\ |4-x| & \ge \sqrt{17}.\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
4-x\le -\sqrt{17}\,\text{or}\,4-x\ge \sqrt{17}
$$

We can solve each inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}4-x & \le -\sqrt{17} &  &  & 4-x & \ge \sqrt{17} \\ -x & \le -\sqrt{17}-4 &  &  & -x & \ge \sqrt{17}-4 \\ x & \ge 4+\sqrt{17} &  &  & x & \le 4-\sqrt{17}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is

$$
x\le 4-\sqrt{17}\,\text{or}\,x\ge 4+\sqrt{17}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+4)^{4}+6 & <18 \\ 2(x+4)^{4} & <12 \\ (x+4)^{4} & <6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take the fourth root of both sides and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[4]{(x+4)^{4}} & <\sqrt[4]{6} \\ |x+4| & <\sqrt[4]{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
-\sqrt[4]{6}<x+4<\sqrt[4]{6}
$$

Now, we can solve the compound inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}-\sqrt[4]{6}<x+4 & <\sqrt[4]{6} \\ -\sqrt[4]{6}-4<x & <\sqrt[4]{6}-4\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality Involving an Even Power Compared To a Negative Number
questions.worked_solution:
Isolating the eighth-degree term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}4(2-x)^{8}+3 & \ge -9 \\ 4(2-x)^{8} & \ge -12 \\ (2-x)^{8} & \ge -3.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $(2-x)^{8}\ge 0$ for all values of $x$ because the power $(8)$ is even.

Therefore, the solution to the given inequality is all real numbers.

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality Involving an Even Power
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Isolating the quartic term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(5x+2)^{4}}{9}-3 & >6 \\ \frac{(5x+2)^{4}}{9} & >9 \\ (5x+2)^{4} & >81.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take the fourth root of both sides and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[4]{(5x+2)^{4}} & >\sqrt[4]{81} \\ |5x+2| & >3.\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
5x + 2 \lt -3 \qquad \textrm{or} \qquad 5x + 2 \gt 3
$$

We can solve each inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+2 & <-3 &  &  & 5x+2 & >3 \\ 5x & <-5 &  &  & 5x & >1 \\ x & <-1 &  &  & x & >\frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
x \lt -1 \quad \textrm{or} \quad x \gt \dfrac{1}{5}.
$$
